base.description: CRS418-8P-8G-2S+RM - 16 Gigabit Ethernet ports (Ether9-16 with PoE out), a Gigabit management port, two SFP+ cages, a USB type A port and the RJ45 console, with two built-in AC supplies and four fans. The box holds two power cords, rack ears and a K-54 fastening set.

description: MikroTik CRS418-8P-8G-2S+RM is a fixed 1U Cloud Router Switch with PoE out and a quad-core ARM CPU. It has 16 Gigabit Ethernet ports in two blocks of eight, of which the second block (Ether9-16) supplies PoE out (802.3af/at, or 24 V passive), a Gigabit management port printed MGMT/BOOT, an RJ45 serial console, two SFP+ cages and a USB type A port, and runs RouterOS v7. The front carries the two jack blocks, the two cages each with an ACT and a 10G lamp, the USB port, the console over the management port, the RESET and MODE buttons, four status lamps and a slanted vent. Two AC inlets, each with its own supply built in, and four fan openings are on the rear. The supplies are part of the chassis, so there are no bays.

gaps.note: The brochure and the product page say USB 3.0 type A. Photograph 2478 shows a white tongue with four contacts, which is the colour and contact count of USB 2.0. The photograph is drawn, with the registry's white-tongue skin.

built-in-power-and-fans.note: The brochure and the page list two AC inputs and two PSU slots. The page counts 4 fans. The rear photograph (2479) shows two C14 inlets, each with a steel retaining clip, and no removable supply, no handle and no part number, so the supplies are part of the chassis and there are no bays, as on juniper/ex2300-24t. Each inlet is the registry's C14 with the rating printed under it, 100-240 V ~1 A MAX 50/60 Hz, carried as printed; the brochure's 215 W is the box's own maximum, the 1 A a per-inlet label. The four round openings are the four fans.

buttons.note: Two round buttons printed RESET and MODE on the metal (the page lists "Mode button: Yes"), drawn with the library's recessed reset-button part; the MODE one carries function mode.

chassis.note: 443 wide, 44 high, 230 deep, as the drawing prints them; the brochure prints 443 x 230 x 44 and agrees. The drawing dimensions 7 mm beyond the body at one end of its top plan, which is the pair of retaining clips of the two AC inlets (photograph 2478 shows them above the far edge of the lid, and photograph 2479 shows them on the rear), and 5.3 mm at the other end, where the SFP+ cages stand proud of the face; neither is part of the 230.

colour.note: median of photograph 2478: face #d6d3d3. The chassis colour is the face's.

datasheet.note: The brochure is MikroTik's datasheet for the model: product code CRS418-8P-8G-2S+RM, quad-core IPQ-8072 2208 MHz ARM 64 bit, 1 GB DDR3L, 128 MB NAND, 17 Gigabit Ethernet ports, two SFP+ ports, one USB 3.0 type A, 98DX226S, RouterOS v7 level 5, 443 x 230 x 44 (no unit printed), -20 to +70 C, two AC inputs, 100-240 V, PoE out 802.3af/at on Ether9-Ether16 (the heading adds 24 V passive), 1.1 A per port at input below 30 V and 0.56 A above, 5.4 A and 150 W total out, 28 W without attachments and 215 W maximum. The product page lists the same, two PSU slots and 4 fans. The brochure calls the case one "with redundant power inputs" and "dual AC inputs"; it states no redundancy form. Each figure is filed as the document words it.

ears.note: Rack ears are in the box (product page: Rack ears; the brochure says "Rackmount bracket"; also 2 power cords and a K-54 kit, a screw set per the intake notes). The drawing's front view and top plan show the body and the two 7 mm inlet clips, with no ear plate, so the ears are shipped flush with the face and drawn at the face plane; they are not drawn.

front-layout.note: From the drawing's front view. Two jack plates 60.5 x 26.7 at 19.6 and 90.1 mm (70.5 mm step), top at 10.4 mm; four columns of two ganged jacks on the 13.97 mm registry pitch, the first jack at 22.55 mm (plate left + 2.95), and a 14.62 mm gutter between the blocks. The rows are read from the drawn jack outlines at centres 17.15 and 30.2 mm, a 13.05 mm pitch. The two SFP+ cages are centred at 168.6 and 186.2 mm (a 17.6 mm pitch: they do not abut), 31.6 mm down, with their 14.5 x 10.0 registry openings; the drawn bezels around them are 17.2 x 12.2. The ACT and 10G lamps are the four ringed circles beside the cages, at 156.3 and 198.4 mm, 28.6 and 34.0 mm. The USB bezel is 8.7 x 16.1 at 210.9 mm, 21.0 mm, standing upright. The console and management jacks share a plate 17.9 x 26.9 at 254.9 mm, 10.2 mm, centred at 263.8 mm and 13.7 mm apart. The RESET and MODE buttons are the two round marks at 277.2 and 286.5 mm, 32.4 mm. The four lamps are a column of rings at 293.8 mm, 17.6, 22.7, 27.8 and 32.8 mm. The slanted vent is 120.2 x 19.5 mm at 313.2 mm, 15.5 mm. The face colour #d6d3d3 is the photograph's.

gate-1.note: The drawing's front view body is 1744 px wide in a 400 dpi render for the printed 443 (3.937 px per mm) and 173 px tall between the lip lines, which reads 43.9 mm, the printed 44. Every x and y below is taken at 3.937 px per mm from the body's top-left corner of the front view.

lamps.note: The four rings in a column are the status lamps; photograph 2478 prints USER, FAULT, PWR 2 and PWR 1 beside them, top to bottom, and shows them as small dark lenses with a green rim, unlit. The ACT and 10G lamps beside each cage are two rings, ACT above and 10G below, as printed. Which cage a lamp pair belongs to is read from its place (the left pair beside SFP+ 1, the right pair beside SFP+ 2). No document says what a lamp shows.

management-and-console.note: Photograph 2478 prints CONSOLE over the upper jack of the shared plate and MGMT/BOOT under the lower. The brochure counts "17 Gigabit Ethernet ports" and describes "a Gigabit management port with a direct CPU line", the 17th; the page lists a serial console port, RJ45. The management jack is filed at 1g.

poe-markings.note: Photograph 2478 shows two lit round lamps left of the second block, a red one and under it a green one beside the legend 28 V, with the legend PoE out and an arrow under them. These are lamps with lit colours, as on the CRS328-24P, and are placed as lamps with the photograph's lit colours (#ef4444 and #22c55e). Over the second block it also shows two plain grey bars, each over a pair of columns, with the numbers 10 12 and 14 16 under them. The drawing shows arrow marks inside each bar (a down and an up arrow for each column), so they are windows, but no photograph shows one lit and no document says what they show, so they are drawn as printed bars, as the CRS354-48P draws what its photograph shows, and not as lamps (gap `poe-lamps`). Positions: the lamps and the legends are read off photograph 2478 at 5.46 px per mm across the face, which looks down on it (x about 1 mm, y about 1.5 mm); the bars are the drawing's, 24.2 x 3.3 mm at 94.3 and 122.2 mm, 4.1 mm. Only the second block, Ether9 to Ether16, supplies PoE out.

port-numbering.note: The metal prints the even numbers over the upper jacks (2 4 6 8 and 10 12 14 16) and the odd numbers under the lower ones (1 3 5 7 and 9 11 13 15), so the lower jack of a column takes the odd number, centred on its column. The cages are printed SFP+ 1 and SFP+ 2. Ether1 to Ether8 are the first block and Ether9 to Ether16 the second (the brochure's PoE-out ports are Ether9 - Ether16).

rear-layout.note: From photograph 2479 (the rear, from above), x across the 443 mm at 5.43 px per mm and y estimated (the photo looks down; the face is 0.82 of its true height). Four fan openings 33 mm across, centred 41.6, 93.1, 287.1 and 351.4 mm and 25.0 mm down. Two inlets, centred 156.0 and 206.6 mm and 19.0 mm down. The photograph reads the two left fans 51.5 mm apart and the right two 64.3 mm apart; this is carried as seen. The retaining clips, the screws at the fans and the legends POWER 1 and POWER 2 partly hidden by the inlets are read to about 2 mm. Seen from behind the first inlet is at the left, as in the photograph.

side-layout.note: estimated - the drawing has no side view. The isometric and photograph 2477 show a small hex vent on the right wall, about a quarter of the way back. It is drawn 24 x 24 mm, 56 mm from the front and 10 mm down, read off the photograph, which looks at the wall obliquely (about 6 mm). The left wall is not shown by any held document.

usb.note: One USB type A port standing upright (page: USB 3.0 type A, 1 A maximum, USB power reset). Photograph 2478 shows a white tongue with four contacts, the colour of a USB 2.0 port, so it is drawn with the registry's white-tongue skin; the brochure and the page say 3.0 (gap `usb-generation`). It is the registry's std/usb-a, turned a quarter turn, in a dark bezel the drawing shows 8.7 x 16.1 mm.
